name: Angel One Ltd
title: Angel One Ltd - 543235 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 broking volumes rebounded (orders +13.3% QoQ to 431m, EB/DAT margin 41.7%, normalised 44.4%), but cash market share fell 117 bps QoQ and management guided only to flat employee cost and a 2.5-3% new-business drag.

summary.headline: Angel One Q4 FY26: gross income up 9.7% QoQ to ₹14.7 bn, net income up 10.4% to ₹11.3 bn, reported EBDAT margin 41.7%.
summary.overview: Orders executed rose 13.3% QoQ to 431 mn despite one fewer trading day, with broking at 60.7% of gross income. Reported EBDAT margin expanded 227 bps QoQ to 41.7%, and normalized margin (ex one-time items and IPL) rose 498 bps to 44.4%. PAT grew 19.2% QoQ to ₹3.2 bn. Management flagged softer distribution revenue (credit and IPO related) and a one-time ₹192 mn client goodwill reimbursement, and proposed capital infusion of up to ₹1.5 bn each into the wealth and NBFC businesses.

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized EBDAT margin (ex one-time and IPL)

segments.name: Broking (Direct + Assisted)
segments.commentary: Commodity broking income up 15.8% QoQ, F&O revenue up 16.1% QoQ, cash segment up 4.6% QoQ. Assisted (AP) channel is about 25-27% of broking revenue; direct about 75%.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue moderated QoQ due to lower credit distribution and softer IPO activity, partly offset by insurance distribution growth. Management called these trends cyclical.

segments.name: Wealth (Ionic Wealth)
segments.commentary: AUM crossed ₹100 bn, up 23% QoQ; UHNI business grew 2x over 12 months; AUM per RM up 3x YoY; over 45% of 1,900+ clients from non-metros. Breakeven guided in about 3-3.5 years.

segments.name: Asset Management (AMC)
segments.commentary: Period-end AUM ₹3.6 bn, down sequentially on softer markets and liquid fund redemptions; folios up 28% QoQ to over 246,000; scheme count 11 after Silver ETF launches.

segments.name: Credit
segments.commentary: Lifetime cumulative disbursements ₹27.1 bn, with ₹6.1 bn disbursed in Q4. Distribution only, no FLDG or credit risk on the books; loan-against-securities to be launched via NBFC on own balance sheet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 employee cost including ESOP expected flat with FY26 (about ₹11 bn); ESOP numbers to be finalized, detail promised for July call.
Operating margin drag from newer businesses for FY26 guided at about 2.5-3%.
Management expects further margin expansion in broking and distribution; cited FY28 margins above 45% but declined to give a specific exit-rate number.
Second half FY26 margin (around 42-43%) to be the base for FY27, per management.
IPL spend for the full season about ₹1.5 bn, with a lower amount booked in Q4 because the season started late in March.
Tax rate expected to move to about 25-26% of PBT as newer businesses scale and deductions reduce.
Cost of acquisition expected to stay in a similar range; no client addition target given.
capex_capacity: Proposed capital infusion of up to ₹1.5 bn each into the wealth management business and the NBFC platform.
Loan-against-securities product to be launched on NBFC balance sheet with pledged AUM as credit limit.
Temporary liquidity arrangements used around the 1 April 2026 banking holiday contributed to elevated borrowings.
Ask Angel AI assistant embedded across app journeys; more than 50% of development augmented by AI; 80% of Ionic Wealth code base AI-generated.
demand_pricing: Average daily orders rose from 5 mn in Feb 2025 to 7.4 mn in Mar 2026; Q4 aggregate 431 mn orders, a six-quarter high.
Retail equity turnover share 20.4%, up 46 bps YoY; demat market share 16.7%, up 54 bps YoY.

Equity market share (cash plus F&O premium) up 46 bps YoY but down 4 bps QoQ; cash share down 117 bps QoQ and 37 bps YoY; F&O premium share up 51 bps QoQ and 77 bps YoY; commodity share up 100 bps QoQ but down YoY.
Cash segment realization fell in Q4; management attributed this to March client mix and sharp market fall, without quantifying.
Management said March saw fewer users returning, with higher-value clients staying active while low-end users exited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the NSE active client count flat despite higher order run rates, and how should customer acquisition costs and cost optimization evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NSE active is a 12-month metric and the industry has started adding net clients again; CAC guided as stable and not disclosed separately. Monthly client acquisitions are disclosed monthly.

qa_highlights.question: What was the ₹192 mn one-time item and is there recourse?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhavin Parekh said a technical issue at the MII level caused an abnormal trading environment; the company paid a goodwill gesture with no obligation. It is working with the MII to recover the amount.

qa_highlights.question: Why did market share in cash fall, and what about commodity yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March drove the cash share dip due to client mix and market fall, with an expected April rebound. Commodity growth was attributed to market expansion, with no structural mix shift seen.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit volume drop seasonal, and is there any FLDG or credit risk on the books?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh Agarwal said the dip is not seasonal, with ecosystem challenges in Q4. No FLDG and no credit risk on the books in the distribution business.

qa_highlights.question: What operating margin drag and breakeven timeline apply to new businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Drag guided at about 2.5-3% for FY26. Wealth breakeven is 3-3.5 years away; management said newer businesses should be evaluated separately from broking.

qa_highlights.question: How does the MTF book behave and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the book unwinds reflect clients bringing their own capital and unpledging, and it does not share return data. Long-term MTF growth expected to be healthy; interest rate outlook not discussed.

risks_watch: One-time ₹192 mn client reimbursement from MII disruption; recovery from the MII is still unresolved.
Higher borrowings and dependence on bank guarantees after RBI directions on banks' capital market exposure; intraday credit may tighten.
Market share in cash segment weakened QoQ; March volatility and retail behavior could weigh on the next quarter.
Credit distribution volumes declined QoQ; management attributes this to ecosystem issues.
Newer businesses drag 2.5-3% on operating margin; investment decisions may keep the margin trajectory uneven.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's operating recovery and margin expansion, but guarded on specifics: management declined to give exit-rate margin, ESOP, MTF rate or CAC numbers and attributed the cash market-share dip and weak credit volumes to March or one-off factors.
key_quotes: Our average daily orders have recovered well , and our operating margins are back within our guided range.
In cash, specifically on cash we are seeing a bit of a dip because of March.
We do not indulge in those loans which are less than ₹50,000, which are the small ticket loans which have seen a lot of risk in the market over the last, say, two to three years.
But you should think of it as the margin expanding further.

growth.why: No top-line revenue guidance; management guided only on costs (FY27 employee cost flat at ~₹11 bn, newer-business margin drag 2.5-3%) and cited a Q4 gross income rise of 9.7% QoQ driven by orders up 13.3% QoQ, with no capacity additions or order-book-type backing for growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Normalized EBDAT margin rose 498 bps QoQ to 44.4% and management cites FY28 margins above 45%, with H2 FY26 margin of about 42-43% as the FY27 base; newer-business drag is 2.5-3% and employee cost is flat at about ₹11 bn.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Wealth AUM crossed ₹100 bn (up 23% QoQ) and a loan-against-securities product is to launch on the NBFC balance sheet, but no physical capacity or plant numbers were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 orders rose 13.3% QoQ to 431 mn, a six-quarter high, and average daily orders rose from 5 mn (Feb 2025) to 7.4 mn (Mar 2026); however, cash share fell 117 bps QoQ and March saw fewer users returning.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Proposed capital infusion of up to ₹1.5 bn each into wealth and NBFC is a firm capital decision, but utilisation is not a relevant metric for this asset-light broker, so no new capex plan is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No top-line guidance was given, and management guided only on costs; the ₹192 mn one-time item and softer distribution revenue argue against a raised outlook.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cash market share fell 117 bps QoQ, credit distribution volumes declined on ecosystem issues, and the ₹192 mn MII reimbursement is unrecovered; a weaker April or margin drag from new businesses could pressure the FY27 base.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Loan-against-securities is to launch via NBFC on the own balance sheet, and the AMC has already added Silver ETFs taking scheme count to 11.

rows.label: Recovery of ₹192 mn MII goodwill reimbursement
rows.why: The company is working with the MII to recover the ₹192 mn paid as a goodwill gesture, but recovery is unresolved and there is no obligation on the MII.

rows.label: Wealth AUM and UHNI scale-up
rows.why: Ionic Wealth AUM crossed ₹100 bn (up 23% QoQ), UHNI business grew 2x over 12 months, and 1,900+ clients with over 45% from non-metros; breakeven still 3-3.5 years away.

rows.label: Borrowing and intraday credit tightening
rows.why: Elevated borrowings from temporary liquidity arrangements around the 1 April 2026 holiday, and RBI directions on bank capital market exposure could tighten intraday credit against ₹54.5 bn client funding book.

tone.note: Management was confident on the operating recovery and FY27 cost guidance (flat ~₹11 bn employee cost, 2.5-3% new-business drag) but declined exit-rate margin, ESOP, MTF rate and CAC numbers, and blamed the cash share dip and weak credit volumes on March or one-off factors; analysts pressed on the ₹
